text.p: Jack Kemp used the front lawn of an internationally known hospital on Monday to praise the U.S. health care system and pledge that it would get even better under his presidential running mate, Bob Dole.

Addressing a crowd estimated at 400-2,000, he also pledged that under a Dole administration, minorities and low-income people would have a better chance at the American Dream because taxes would be lower and the economy would expand.
Ohio, with 21 electoral votes, is considered a crucial state for Dole, who is scheduled to visit the state on Tuesday.

The Republican vice presidential nominee saluted the Cleveland Clinic Foundation and said, "This is truly the type of system that can be spread all over this country if we make sure it is predicated upon those public-private partnerships, not the government takeover of health care in the United States of America," Kemp said.

Deriding President Bill Clinton's failed health-care reform plan, Kemp said, "The reason 80 different countries send men and women to the Cleveland health-care clinic or to (other U.S. hospitals) is because they know that in the United States of America, you can get the best health care anywhere in the world.
"We can make it even better under Bob Dole as the next President of the United States of America," he said, pledging free choice of medical facilities and doctors under a public-private partnership.
Citing polls that indicate 55 percent of Americans say they are doing well economically, Kemp said he and Dole would fight for the other 45 percent.
"We want to make it work for everybody -- black, white, brown, immigrant, native born. This is America. We must come together," he said.

"We must build a ladder of opportunity upon which all people can climb, and that will not come until we expand this economy far more than just the anaemic level of growth that we are enjoying today in the United States of America," he said.
Local Democrats were sceptical of Kemp's health care remarks. Cuyahoga County Commissioner Mary Boyle said Kemp provided no specifics on a Dole-Kemp health care plan.
"He didn't answer who's going to pay for it," she said. "The plan they talk about is wonderful if you happen to have health insurance. If you don't have health insurance, it doesn't work."
